problems.title: An impossible congruence
problems.question: How many integer solutions has 27x≡1(mod 9)?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: 27x is divisible by 9 for every integer x.
steps: It therefore has remainder0 and cannot have remainder1.

problems.title: Compute a recurrence
problems.question: a₁=2 and aₙ₊₁=3aₙ−1. Find a₅.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Apply the recurrence successively.
steps: a₂=5, a₃=14, a₄=41, and a₅=122.

problems.title: Largest sequence term
problems.question: Find the largest term of aₙ=12−n²+8n, n natural.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
steps: The maximum is 28, attained at n=4.

problems.title: Arc between neighbouring hexagon vertices
problems.question: A regular hexagon has shorter diagonal6√3. Find the circumcircle arc length between adjacent vertices.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Short diagonal=√3 times the side, so side=radius=6. The adjacent central angle is π/3.
steps: Arc length=Rθ=6·π/3=2π.

problems.title: Tangent-chord angle and a sector
problems.question: AB is tangent at A, C lies on the circle, and∠CAB=30°. How many times larger is the disk are a than the minor AOC sector are a?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The tangent-chord theorem gives minor central angle AOC=60°.
steps: The sector is 60/360=1/6 of the disk. The requested ratio is 6.

problems.title: Select a congruence root
problems.question: Which listed x solves15x≡21(mod 18)?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Divide by 3:5x≡7(mod 6), equivalent to x≡5(mod 6).
steps: Among60,69,70,71,75,87, only 71 has remainder5 modulo6.

problems.title: Two possible ratios from a factored condition
problems.question: Given xy/(x²+6y²)=1/5, which listed value can xy/(x²−6y²) have?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: x²−5xy+6y²=(x−2y)(x−3y)=0. The original quotient ensures y≠0.
steps: If x=2y, the target is −1. If x=3y, it is 1. Of these, only 1 is listed.
problems.answer: 1 among the choices; the other possible value is −1.

problems.title: Compare powers of one base
problems.question: Order a=27^(1/4), b=9^(2/7), c=⁵√81, d=⁹√(3⁵).
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: They are powers of 3 with exponents3/4,4/7,4/5,5/9, respectively.
steps: Since 5/9<4/7<3/4<4/5, the order is d<b<a<c.

problems.title: Overlap of equal circles
problems.question: Two equal circles each pass through the other’s centre. Radius is √3. Find overlap are a.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The lens consists of 2 sectors of 120°, minus2 equilateral triangles of side R.
steps: Area=2[(120/360)πR²−√3R²/4]. With R²=3, this is 2π−3√3/2.

problems.title: Circle inscribed in a sector
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in a sector of angle 2α radians. Find sector are a/circle are a.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Let sector radius R, small-circle radius r. Its centre is r/sinα from the vertex, so R=r(1+sinα)/sinα.
steps: Sector are a=αR², circle are a=πr². Divide and substitute R/r.
problems.note: This uses the standard sector with 0<2α≤π and the circle tangent to both radial sides and the arc.

problems.title: Count bounded sequence terms
problems.question: How many terms of aₙ=n²−7n+18 lie in[−1,8]?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The lower bound is automatic because aₙ=(n−3.5)²+5.75. The upper bound gives n²−7n+10≤0.
steps: Factor(n−2)(n−5)≤0. The natural indices are 2,3,4,5, so there are 4.

problems.title: Pair two reciprocal radical factors
problems.question: Evaluate[∛(√3+√6)·⁶√(9−6√2)−∛24]/∛3.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
steps: Their indicated radical product is∛3·∛[(1+√2)(√2−1)]=∛3. Also∛24=2∛3.
The full quotient is(∛3−2∛3)/∛3=−1.

problems.title: Which universal statements hold?
problems.question: Check:I Σ1/[(4j−3)(4j+1)]=n/(3n+2); II5 divides n⁵−n; IIIΣj(3j−1)=n²(n+1); IVevery integer amount>7 uses3- and 5-unit notes.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: I telescopes to n/(4n+1), so its printed formula is false. II follows by testing the 5 residue classes modulo5.
steps: III follows from 3Σj²−Σj=n²(n+1). IV holds for 8=3+5,9=3+3+3,10=5+5, and then adding3 proves every larger integer case.
Thus precisely II, III, IV are true.

problems.title: Smallest disk containing an obtuse triangle
problems.question: Find the are a of the smallest disk containing a triangle with sides 7,9,12.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: 12²>7²+9², so the triangle is obtuse. The smallest enclosing circle of an obtuse triangle has its longest side as diameter.
steps: Its radius is 12/2=6, and disk are a 36π.

problems.title: Disk portion inside an inscribed angle
problems.question: Equal chords AB, AC for m∠BAC=30°. Find disk are a divided by the disk portion inside that angle.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The minor arc BC is 60°. With radius R, the triangle ABC are a is R²(2+√3)/4, and the minor BC segment are a is R²(π/6−√3/4).
steps: Their sum is R²(π+3)/6. Divide disk are a πR² by this sum.

problems.title: A listed positive-root parameter
problems.question: Which listed a makes x²−(2a+1)x+a²−7a+6=0 have only positive real roots?
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Need discriminant32a−23≥0, root sum 2a+1>0, and product(a−1)(a−6)>0.
steps: Together the valid a-set is[23/32,1)∪(6,∞). Of1,2,3,4,6,7, only 7 belongs.

problems.title: Smallest cubic-sequence term
problems.question: Find the smallest term of xₙ=(n+1)(n−5)(n−8), n natural.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: For n≤5 and n≥8, the product is nonnegative. Only n=6,7 can be negative.
steps: x₆=−14, x₇=−16. The minimum is −16.

problems.title: Largest parameter with positive roots
problems.question: Find the largest k for which every root of(k−3)x²−2kx+6k=0 is positive.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: For a quadratic, the positive-root conditions are k/(k−3)>0 and discriminant4k(18−5k)≥0.
steps: These give3<k≤18/5. At k=3, the equation becomes linear with positive root 3, so it also works.
The maximum remains18/5, where the repeated root is 6.
problems.note: A root is required to exist; the quadratic discriminant condition prevents vacuous acceptance of parameters with no real roots.

problems.title: An integer bound for nested radicals
problems.question: Find the least natural M bounding the sequence yₙ=√(7+√(7+…)), with n radical levels.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: y₁=√7<4, and yₙ<4 implies yₙ₊₁=√(7+yₙ)<√11<4.
steps: Thus 4 bounds every term. But y₂=√(7+√7)>3, so 3 does not. The least integer bound is 4.

problems.title: A chord divides a disk
problems.question: A chord divides its circle into arcs in ratio1:11. Find the ratio of the two disk parts.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The smaller arc is 30°. Its segment are a is sector minus triangle:R²(π/12−1/4)=R²(π−3)/12.
steps: The other segment are a is πR² minus this, or R²(11π+3)/12. Divide the two.

problems.title: A square inside a30° sector
problems.question: A sector radius √13, angle 30°, contains a square with 2 vertices on OA, one on OB, and one on the arc. Find square are a.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: Let square side s and OA horizontal. The nearer bottom vertex has x=s cot30°=s√3. The far upper vertex is(s(√3+1), s).
steps: Its squared distance from O is s²[(√3+1)²+1]=s²(5+2√3)=13.

problems.title: A parameter question with a continuum of answers
problems.question: Find the product of all a-values for which every root of 3ax²+(3a³−12a²−1)x−a(a−4)=0 satisfies|x|<1.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The polynomial factors as(3ax−1)[x+a(a−4)]. At a=0, it is −x, so the sole root 0 qualifies.
steps: For a≠0, the roots are 1/(3a) and a(4−a). Require|a|>1/3 and|a(a−4)|<1. The resulting set is(2+√3,2+√5).
Including the linear case, the full set is{0}∪(2+√3,2+√5). It is not a finite set, so its ordinary finite product is not defined.
problems.answer: Full parameter set:{0}∪(2+√3,2+√5); no finite product as stated.
problems.note: If the intended question restricted a to integers, the valid values would be 0,4 and their product 0, the listed likely intended answer. The printed source does not state that restriction.

problems.title: Use a given radical-square identity
problems.question: Let u=∛2, v=⁴√3 and u²+v²=(u+v−a)². Simplify[u²+(u−a)²]/[v²+(v−a)²].
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: The given relation is equivalent to a²=2(u−a)(v−a).
steps: The numerator becomes2(u−a)(u+v−a); the denominator becomes2(v−a)(u+v−a).
Their common nonzero factor cancels, leaving(u−a)/(v−a).

problems.title: A curved region in a cyclic trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid’s circumcentre lies on its base AD=12 and∠ADC=60°. Find the region bounded by AB, AC, and minor arc BC.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: AD is a diameter, so R=6. A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles; coordinates may be A=(−6,0), D=(6,0), B=(−3,3√3), C=(3,3√3).
steps: Triangle ABC are a is 9√3. Arc BC has central angle 60°, so its segment are a is 6π−9√3.
The requested region is their sum 6π.

problems.title: Largest-area sector with fixed perimeter
problems.question: A sector has perimeter2m. Find the central angle of the maximum-are a sector.
problems.idea: Use modular arithmetic, root identities, and circle-are a formulas; retain all parameter cases.
formulas: If its radius is r and arc length l, then2r+l=2m. Area=rl/2=r(m−r)=m²/4−(r−m/2)².
steps: The maximum occurs at r=m/2, l=m. Its angle is l/r=2 radians.
